entries.title: Advocacy notify dialog lets you email only new campaign recipients
entries.summary: When sending notifications on a campaign that has already been emailed, the **Notify** dialog now offers two choices: **Everyone (N)** to re-send to all recipients, or **Only new (M)** to reach only people added since the last send. The counts come from a live dry run so you always know exactly how many people will receive the message before you confirm.
entries.use_case: Campaigns that grow over time — such as rolling attendee invitations — previously required organizers to manually track who had already been notified to avoid duplicate emails. The **Only new** option lets organizers safely re-open the notify dialog at any point and send only to people who haven't received the campaign email yet.

cs_action.note: Requires the companion API change in lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4584. Until that API ships, the dry-run call returns a 400, the Only new option stays hidden, and Notify behaves as before — no customer impact during the gap.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running a rolling Advocacy campaign asks how to avoid re-emailing people who already received a campaign notification.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy campaigns where recipients are added in batches over time.
internal.gotchas: The Only new option is hidden until the API (web-api#4584) is deployed. Deploy order is safe — no regression if the UI ships first.
internal.talk_track: Once your campaign has been sent, the Notify dialog will show you two options: resend to everyone, or reach only the people added since your last send — with exact counts so you know what you're about to do.

entries.title: Campaign emails now include the event logo
entries.summary: Campaign emails, test sends, automated sends, and workflow sends were delivered without the event logo when no email theme was set. All sends now wrap the email body in the same template used by **Send Email**, so the event logo (or org logo for org-scoped sends) appears consistently.
entries.use_case: Events that rely on campaigns to communicate with speakers and attendees expect branded emails. The logo now appears in every campaign send without requiring a theme to be configured.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer notices their campaign emails look unbranded or are missing the event logo.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using email campaigns without a custom email theme set — particularly common for events that have not configured themes.
internal.gotchas: This fix applies retroactively to all future sends; previously sent emails are not resent. Org-scoped sends use the org logo; event-scoped sends use the event logo.
internal.talk_track: Campaign emails now automatically include your event logo in the same branded wrapper as your other emails, even if you haven't set up a custom email theme.

entries.title: Session fields and participant details no longer appear blank in printed booklets
entries.summary: Selected session fields, participant titles, and company names were blank in every printed booklet because the locale code was stored as `en_US` but looked up as `en-US`. The event's configured language is now used with the correct format, so all field values appear as expected.
entries.use_case: Organizers who generate printed program books rely on session fields and speaker details being populated. This fix ensures those values appear correctly without any manual workaround.

cs_action.note: Any customer who generated a booklet after PR #4495 (recent release) may have a blank-field booklet saved. Proactively reach out to customers who use Print Agendas and suggest they regenerate.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that session fields, speaker titles, or company names are missing from their printed booklet or program book.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Print Agendas / booklet feature — regression affected all booklets since a recent release.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Print → open a booklet → regenerate
internal.gotchas: Booklets generated between PR #4495 and this fix will still show blank fields until the customer regenerates them. Friendly ID and Client Session ID now pull from their dedicated Sessions columns.
internal.talk_track: A recent update accidentally caused session fields and speaker details to go blank in printed booklets. That is now fixed — just regenerate your booklet and everything will appear correctly.

entries.title: Draft submissions now save all session fields, not just the title
entries.summary: When a speaker saved a submission as a draft, only the **Title** was written to the draft session record — **Description**, other standard fields, and every custom field answer were silently dropped. All standard columns and custom field values are now saved on every draft save, so speakers can resume a draft and find their work intact.
entries.use_case: Speakers who fill in a description, custom answers, and other fields before saving a draft no longer lose that work. They can return to the draft and pick up exactly where they left off.

cs_action.note: Fix is automatic; no action needed. 3,417 US and 389 EU drafts were affected — those speakers will see their previously missing fields restored on next load.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A speaker reports that their draft lost everything except the title, or an organizer notices draft sessions with only a title and no other content.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer whose speakers use the Save as Draft feature on submission forms.
internal.gotchas: If a session Description was edited directly on the session record after the draft was saved, the newer session-record value wins over the snapshot on resume — this is intentional.
internal.talk_track: Speakers can now save a draft at any point and come back to find all their answers — title, description, and every custom field — exactly as they left them.

entries.title: Speaker feedback can use Evaluation Plan 2.0 reviews
entries.summary: The speaker-portal **Evaluation reviews** source only listed v1 evaluation plans. Evaluation Plan 2.0 plans are now offered too: each session is scored from its last round with a completed review, shown out of 5 and pooled with any v1 plan on the same scale. A reviewer on both a v1 and a v2 plan counts once toward the minimum number of reviews.

where.path: Event Settings → Record Settings → Speaker portal → Evaluation reviews

entries.use_case: Events running Evaluation Plan 2.0 can finally share reviewer scores with their speakers in the portal.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Events running Evaluation Plan 2.0 can finally share reviewer scores with their speakers in the portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using this area; no action needed.
internal.staff_path: Event Settings → Record Settings → Speaker portal → Evaluation reviews
internal.gotchas: Plan 2.0 has no reviewer note for submitters, so v2 plans add scores but no notes. Sessions below the minimum number of reviews show no score.
internal.talk_track: Events running Evaluation Plan 2.0 can finally share reviewer scores with their speakers in the portal.
